title: Juncus tenuis

Path rush (USA) |image = Jute 002 lvp.jpg |genus = Juncus |species = tenuis |authority = [[Carl Ludwig Willdenow|Willd.]] }} '''''Juncus tenuis''''', the '''slender rush''', is a clump-forming, round-stemmed perennial in the [[Juncaceae]] (rush [[Family (taxonomy)|family]]). Native to North America and introduced to Europe, Australia, and parts of Asia, slender rush grows to be between 15 and 60 cm tall.{{Cite web |title=Juncus tenuis (Path Rush, Poverty Rush, Rush, Slender Rush) {{!}} North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox |url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/juncus-tenuis/ |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=plants.ces.ncsu.edu}} Generally considered a [[weed]], it is rarely sold by retailers as a household container plant. Where it is introduced, it is colloquially called '''path rush''', '''field rush''', '''slender yard rush''', '''poverty rush''' or '''wiregrass'''. The [[leaves]] of the plant all come from the base and are not nearly as tall as the stems. The stems are partly covered by sheaths, and have the most distinctive characteristic of the plant on them: clusters or [[Cyme (botany)|cymes]] at the top. These cymes consist of branches that have small egg-shaped seed capsules at the end of them. The seeds split into three parts when they become ripe. The plant also spreads via rhizomatous root growth. == Habitat == Slender rush grows in landscapes, [[agriculture|crops]], roadsides, and all types of fields. It can grow on both wet and dry sites, in soils consisting mainly of sand or clay. Because of its high tolerance of compacted soils, it can outcompete other plant species in such places, hence the name "path rush". It is native throughout all fifty states of United States, most of Canada, and parts of northern [[Europe]]. == References == {{Reflist}} * {{cite book |first=Richard H. |last=Uva |first2=Joseph C. |last2=Neal |first3=Joseph M. |last3=Ditomaso |title=Weeds of The Northeast |location=Ithaca, NY |publisher=Cornell University Press |year=1997 |pages=28–29 |isbn=0-8014-3391-6 }} * USDA | NRCS, [https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=JUTE Plants Profile for ''Juncus tenuis''] * Missouri Botanical Garden, [http://www.mobot.org/gardinghelp/plantfinder/plant.asp?code=Q200 ''Juncus tenuis''] * Dr. John Hilty, [http://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/grasses/plants/path_rush.htm Path Rush] * Niche Gardens, [http://www.nichegardens.com/catalog/item.php?id=2222 ''Juncus tenuis''] * eFloras, [http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=222000181 Path rush] == External links == {{Commonscat-inline|Juncus tenuis}} * Jim Lindsey, [http://www.commanster.eu/commanster/Plants/Grasses/SuGrasses/Juncus.tenuis.html Photo images of ''Juncus tenuis von Willdenow'' ] {{Taxonbar|from=Q148097}} [[Category:Juncus|tenuis]] [[Category:Flora of Northern America]] [[Category:Flora of Europe]] [[Category:Plants described in 1799]]
